en.title: The Book of De · Chapter Fifteen · Keeping to the Mother
en.原文:
天下有始
以為天下母

𢟪得亓母
以知亓子
復守亓母
沒身不殆

塞亓悶
閉亓門
終身不堇

啟亓悶
濟亓事
終身不棘

見小曰眀
守柔曰強

用亓光
復歸亓明

毋道身央
是胃襲常
en.字龕:
### 母 *mǔ* — mother

**字 Graph** ｜ 篆 ![母之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E6%AF%8D.svg)

**文 Gloss** ｜ The *Shuowen*: 「牧也。從女，象褱子形。一曰象乳子也。」 — "To tend and nourish. From 女, the woman, in the posture of embracing a child; some say the two dots picture the breasts that nurse it."

**像 Image** ｜ A woman with a child held in — or the two points that feed it. The graph does not picture ancestry; it pictures nourishing.

**義 Sense** ｜ The Dao as "mother of all-under-heaven" is mother in exactly this sense: not the founder far back at the start of the line, but the one still feeding everything now. That is why one can *return* to her and keep her.

### 守 *shǒu* — keeping

**字 Graph** ｜ 篆 ![守之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E5%AE%88.svg)

**文 Gloss** ｜ The *Shuowen*: 「守，守官也。從宀從寸。寺府之事者。從寸。寸，法度也。」 — "To keep an office. From 宀, the roof, and 寸, the measure: the bureau's business kept under a roof, by rule."

**像 Image** ｜ Under a roof, a hand holding the measure. 守 is not a barred gate; it is stewardship — something held in trust, by rule, at home.

**義 Sense** ｜ To "return and keep to the mother" is to come back under that roof and take up the measure again. The keeping is a discipline, not a hiding.

en.校記:
This chapter follows Manuscript A (MS A); where MS A is damaged (以知亓子, 見小曰眀) it is supplied from Manuscript B (MS B), and 終身不棘 combines the two. Graphs are those outside the brackets in the *Changsha Mawangdui Han mu jianbo jicheng* (2014; hereafter *Jicheng*).

- 天下有始: Both manuscripts agree. MS A opens the chapter with a chapter-division dot. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 21, n. 76)
- 𢟪得亓母: Follows MS A, which writes 既 in a variant form, read as 既; MS B writes 既, after which the scribe first miscopied 得 and then circled it out in black ink. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 201, n. 61)
- 以知亓子: 子 is lost in MS A and supplied from MS B. Wang Bi follows with the line 既知其子, and MS B too has 既知亓子, but MS A never had it; the original editors took it as an omission, and the *Jicheng* supplies it with the sign for omitted text. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 21, n. 79)
- 沒身不殆: Follows MS A; MS B writes 佁 for 殆.
- 塞亓悶: Follows MS A, which places a chapter-division dot before this line, thus dividing the received chapter 52 into two. MS B writes 㙂 for 悶; Wang Bi has 兌 "openings". (*Jicheng* IV, p. 21, n. 76)
- 終身不堇: Follows MS A; MS B writes 冬 for 終. Wang Bi reads 終身不勤.
- 啟亓悶 / 濟亓事: Follows MS A; MS B writes 㙂 for 悶 and 齊 for 濟. MS B's 事 was bracketed as a restoration in the 1980 edition; the *Jicheng* reads it directly from the tip of its surviving vertical stroke. Wang Bi reads 開其兌，濟其事. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 201, n. 64)
- 終身不棘: In MS A the two graphs after 終身 are lost; the original editors restored 不棘 from MS B, but the *Jicheng*, noting that MS A has 濟亓事 just above, expects a word of the 不救 kind rhyming with 事 and replaces the restored 棘 with □. MS B reads 冬□不棘, 冬 being read as 終; the 1980 edition restored 終身 at the head of the lower half of the line, whereas the *Jicheng* reads 冬 at the foot of the upper half from a fragment stuck to the backing silk. Wang Bi reads 終身不救. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 22, n. 82; p. 201, n. 65)
- 見小曰眀: Follows MS B, which writes 眀 with the eye radical; MS A keeps only 小曰, and with 見 lost it cannot be known whether a chapter-division dot stood before it. Wang Bi has 明. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 21, n. 76)
- 守柔曰強: Follows MS A; in MS B 柔 is lost, and 曰, bracketed as a restoration in the 1980 edition, is now read directly from the offset on the backing silk. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 201, n. 66)
- 用亓光 / 復歸亓明: Both manuscripts agree, MS B writing 眀 for 明. The 1980 edition restored these six graphs in MS B as 其光 and 復歸其明; the *Jicheng* reads them from the offset on the backing silk. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 201, nn. 67, 68)
- 毋道身央: Follows MS A, whose 道 is a miswriting of 遺, printed 道〈遺〉 in the *Jicheng*. MS B reads 毋遺身央; its 毋, restored as 无 in the 1980 edition, is read as 毋 from the offset, and the graph after it is, in Chen Jian's view, a false start on 央 anticipated from below, left unfinished and circled out. 央 is read as 殃 "calamity"; Wang Bi reads 無遺身殃. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 201, n. 69)
- 是胃襲常: Both manuscripts agree; MS B's 襲, bracketed as a restoration in the 1980 edition, is now read directly from the offset. Wang Bi reads 是為習常. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 201, n. 70)
en.疏:
杳眇曰：

道之為物，生天生地，萬物所從出也。「天下有始，以為天下母」——始者本之時，母者本之親，明道為萬物之本源，萬物稟道而生，循道而終，此之謂也。

「𢟪得亓母，以知亓子，復守亓母，沒身不殆」——此言知本守本之道也。得母即知子，然得子不可忘母；知子而不守母，則逐末忘本；守母而不知子，則孤存於一偏。必兩行而後全。《易》曰「原始反終」，與此歸根復命之旨相發明焉。值得細辨者，帛書甲本作「𢟪得亓母，以知亓子，復守亓母」，三句相承，義已完足；乙本及王弼本增「既知亓子」（王弼作「其」）四字，反覆言之，明暢則明暢矣，然簡淨不如帛書，斧鑿之痕隱然可見。

「塞亓悶，閉亓門，終身不堇」——悶讀為兌（乙本作「㙂」），兌者口也耳目也，門者心所出入。塞兌閉門，非絕外物，乃不為外物所役，老子非教人聾瞎，乃教人以心為主而不以耳目為主。帛書「不堇」即「不勤」，心不外馳則身不疲悴。反之，「啟亓悶，濟亓事，終身不棘」（「終身」下甲本殘，從乙本）——棘讀為救，開情欲、逐事務，終身至於不可救，此為塞閉之反，學者可不戒哉。

「見小曰明，守柔曰強」——見小非由大而及小，乃於小即見道，世人輕微末而重顯赫，聖人於一葉一露見道運。守柔非柔弱之謂，乃容萬變而不折之體，《道德經》稱水之性就下而能攻堅，正此意也。

「用其光，復歸其明」——光者外照之用，明者內藏之體，有光而不歸明者，散之而已；用光而歸明者，動而有靜，是體用相歸之妙。末云「毋遺身殃，是謂襲常」——尤可辨者，帛書作「襲」，王弼本作「習」。襲者承傳之義，示道之代代相承；習者溫習之義，示於恆理之修習。襲字義更深遠，蓋道非一人一時之私，乃百世以俟聖人而不惑者。守母者，此章之要也。夫守母者知本，知本者不殆，修身治世之道，胥在是焉。
en.疏英:
Yaomiao says:

The Dao as a thing gives birth to heaven and to earth; it is what the ten thousand things come out from. "All-under-heaven has a beginning: take it for the mother of all-under-heaven": 始 is the root in time, 母 the root in kinship: the Dao is the wellspring of the ten thousand things, which receive it to be born and follow it to their end.

"Having got the mother, know the children by her; then return and keep to the mother — and to the end of the body, no peril." This is the way of knowing the root and keeping the root. Getting the mother, one knows the children; but getting the children, one must not forget the mother. To know the children without keeping the mother is to chase the tips and lose the root; to keep the mother without knowing the children is to stay confined to one side. Only the double movement makes the whole. The Changes says "trace the beginning, return to the end", which sheds light on, and takes light from, the teaching of returning to the root and to what is ordained. Worth fine attention: silk manuscript A runs 𢟪得亓母，以知亓子，復守亓母, three clauses in file, the sense already complete; manuscript B and the Wang Bi recension insert a fourth, 既知亓子 (Wang Bi: 既知其子), saying it over again. Clearer, yes — but not the silk text's cleanness, and the chisel-mark shows.

"Stop the openings, shut the doors, and to the end of your days you will not be worn." The openings (兌 — manuscript A writes 悶, manuscript B 㙂, both read as 兌) are mouth, ears, eyes; the door is where the heart goes out and in. Stopping and shutting is not cutting off the outer world; it is not being conscripted by it. Laozi does not teach deafness and blindness; he teaches making the heart the master and not the ears and eyes. The silk text's 不堇 is 不勤: a heart not galloping outward, a body not worn down. And the reverse: "open the openings, pursue the affairs, and to the end of your days you will be past saving": the close is lost in manuscript A; manuscript B has 不棘, and 棘 is read as 救. Fling open the appetites, chase the business, until nothing can save you. Let the student take the warning.

"To see the small is called seeing-clear; to keep to the soft is called strength." Seeing the small is not working down from the large; it is seeing the Dao right in the small. The world slights the minute and worships the conspicuous; the sage sees the Dao's operation in one leaf, one bead of dew. Keeping to the soft is no weakness; it is the body that receives ten thousand changes and does not snap — as water's nature runs downward yet bores through the hard.

"Use the shining, then return home to the clear." 光 is the outward-shining use; 明 is the inward-stored substance. To shine without returning to the clear is mere dispersal; to use the shine and come home to the clear is motion that keeps its stillness — the subtlety of use returning to substance. And the close: "leave no calamity on the body — this is called 襲常." Mark the graph: the silk text writes 襲, to inherit, where Wang Bi writes 習, to practice. 襲 is transmission: the Dao handed down generation to generation; 習 is rehearsal — one man's drill at a constant rule. 襲 runs deeper and farther, for the Dao is no one man's and no one age's private thing: it is what awaits a sage a hundred generations hence and is not confounded. Keeping to the mother: that is this chapter's crux. To keep the mother is to know the root; knowing the root, no peril: the way of tending the self and ordering the world is all in this.
en.英譯:
All-under-heaven has a beginning: take it for the mother of all-under-heaven.

Having got the mother, know the children by her; then return and keep to the mother, and to the end of the body there is no peril.

Stop the openings (悶, read as 兌), shut the doors, and to the end of your days you will not be worn. Open the openings, pursue the affairs, and to the end of your days you will be past saving.

To see the small is called seeing-clear (眀); to keep to the soft is called strength.

Use the shining (光), then return home to the clear (明), and leave no calamity on the body: this is called inheriting the constant (襲常).

校記:
本章帛書原文據甲本，甲殘者（「以知亓子」「見小曰眀」）據乙本補，「終身不棘」甲乙相參；字從《集成》（2014）括號外原字。

- 天下有始：甲乙同。甲本章首有分章圓點。（《集成》肆·頁21·注76）
- 𢟪得亓母：從甲本，甲本「既」字作異體，讀為「既」；乙本作「既」，其下原誤抄「得」字，後以黑筆圈去作廢。（《集成》肆·頁201·注61）
- 以知亓子：甲本「子」字殘，據乙本補。王弼本此下有「既知其子」一句，乙本亦有「既知亓子」四字，甲本原件無之；原注以為脫文，《集成》以補脫文之號補出。（《集成》肆·頁21·注79）
- 沒身不殆：從甲本；乙本「殆」作「佁」。
- 塞亓悶：從甲本，句首有分章圓點，是甲本分今本五十二章為二章。乙本「悶」作「㙂」，王弼本作「兌」。（《集成》肆·頁21·注76）
- 終身不堇：從甲本；乙本「終」作「冬」。王弼本作「終身不勤」。
- 啟亓悶　濟亓事：從甲本；乙本「悶」作「㙂」，「濟」作「齊」，其「事」字原釋文作補文，《集成》以尚存直豎之端逕釋。王弼本作「開其兌，濟其事」。（《集成》肆·頁201·注64）
- 終身不棘：甲本「終身」下二字殘，原整理者據乙本補作「不棘」；《集成》以甲本上文作「濟亓事」，此處當用「不救」一類與「事」押韻之字，改補「棘」為「□」。乙本作「冬□不棘」，「冬」讀為「終」，原釋文補「終身」於下截之首，《集成》據襯頁所粘殘片於上截下端釋出「冬」。王弼本作「終身不救」。（《集成》肆·頁22·注82；頁201·注65）
- 見小曰眀：從乙本，作目旁之「眀」；甲本唯存「小曰」，「見」字已殘，其上有無分章圓點不可知。王弼本作「明」。（《集成》肆·頁21·注76）
- 守柔曰強：從甲本；乙本「柔」字殘，「曰」字原為補文，《集成》據襯頁反印文直接釋出。（《集成》肆·頁201·注66）
- 用亓光　復歸亓明：甲乙同，乙本「明」作「眀」。乙本此六字原釋文補作「其光」「復歸其明」，《集成》據襯頁反印文釋出。（《集成》肆·頁201·注67、68）
- 毋道身央：從甲本。甲本「道」為「遺」之誤字，《集成》正作「道〈遺〉」；乙本作「毋遺身央」，「毋」原釋文補作「无」，《集成》據反印文釋「毋」，其下一字，陳劍以為涉下「央」誤抄未全而圈去作廢者。「央」讀為「殃」，王弼本作「無遺身殃」。（《集成》肆·頁201·注69）
- 是胃襲常：甲乙同；乙本「襲」字原為補文，《集成》據反印文直接釋出。王弼本作「是為習常」。（《集成》肆·頁201·注70）
